label: Point of view
description: The point of view of the book, or of one part of it: whose perspective the narration follows, in which person, how close it sits to their thoughts and what it may know. Tense and the prose surface belong to prose style.

fields.label: Viewpoint characters
fields.help: The characters whose perspective the narration follows, one per item, or the narrator alone when the telling follows no single character.

fields.label: Span covered
fields.help: How much of the book this point of view governs, so that a part told differently can be read against the book-wide arrangement.

fields.label: Grammatical person
fields.help: Whether the narration is in first, second or third person, or a planned mix, and which person each viewpoint uses where they differ.

fields.label: Who tells the story
fields.help: Who does the telling, which may differ from whose perspective is followed, and whether that teller has a presence of their own on the page.

options.label: An outside narrator with a presence
Documents or records in the story

fields.label: Moment of telling
fields.help: Where the teller stands in time relative to the events, which decides how much hindsight the narration carries; tense belongs to prose style.

options.label: Not fixed at any one moment

fields.label: Narrative distance
fields.help: How close the narration usually sits to a viewpoint character's thoughts and feelings, from an outside view to inside their head.

fields.label: Planned shifts in distance
fields.help: Where the narration deliberately moves closer to or further from its usual distance, and what each shift is meant to do for the reader.

fields.label: Perceptual lens
fields.help: How seeing through each viewpoint character bends what the narration notices, names and misreads, given what that character knows and overlooks.

fields.label: Limits of knowledge
fields.help: What the narration may know beyond the viewpoint's own experience, what it keeps back from the reader, and what it reveals and when.

fields.label: What the reader knows
fields.help: Whether the reader usually knows more than, as much as or less than the viewpoint character, which decides how suspense and surprise work.

options.label: Reader knows more than the viewpoint
Reader knows as much as the viewpoint
Reader knows less than the viewpoint

fields.label: Narrator reliability
fields.help: How far the reader can trust the narration's account of events, given the teller's errors, biases or deliberate deceptions.

fields.label: Viewpoint switching
fields.help: When and how the narration moves from one viewpoint to another, for instance by chapter or by scene, or a note that it never does.

fields.label: Reason for these viewpoints
fields.help: Why the story is best told through these eyes, in this person and at this distance, and what a different choice would gain or lose.

fields.label: Viewpoint risks
fields.help: Ways the narration could break its own limits, such as knowing what no viewpoint could or drifting between minds mid-scene, one per item.
